<description>
The node raises the unknown rules warning, and runs the `-alertnotify` command, twice in this test. The first time is when the unknown deployment becomes active, and the second is after the restart. The test checks the alert file only once, at the end. As the command appends to the alert file, that check is already satisfied by the output of the first alert, so the test does not wait for the second command at all.

The first commit waits for the first alert before the restart.

The second commit empties the alert file while the node is down, so that the final check can only be satisfied by the second alert.

On Windows, this narrows a race in which the test directory was removed while the second command was still starting. The command keeps open the handles it inherits from the node, which made the cleanup fail:
```
PermissionError: [WinError 32] The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process:...
```

This PR improves the test logic and mitigates https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/28529. However, it does not address the inheritance of the node's handles by child processes, part of which is tracked in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36668.
</description>

<commits>
6315c77592 test: Check the first alert in `feature_versionbits_warning.py`

The node raises the unknown rules warning and runs `-alertnotify` as
soon as the unknown deployment becomes active, which happens before the
restart. Wait for the warning to appear in the alert file at that point.

61ceda1347 test: Wait for the second alert in `feature_versionbits_warning.py`

The check at the end of the test was already satisfied by the output of
the first alert, so the test did not wait for the `-alertnotify` command
run after the restart. Empty the alert file while the node is down, so
that only the second alert can satisfy it.

On Windows, this narrows a race in which the test directory was removed
while that command was still starting. The command keeps open the
handles it inherits from the node, which made the cleanup fail with
WinError 32.
</commits>

diff --git a/test/functional/feature_versionbits_warning.py b/test/functional/feature_versionbits_warning.py
index f630f78172..961abdfd7d 100755
--- a/test/functional/feature_versionbits_warning.py
+++ b/test/functional/feature_versionbits_warning.py
@@ -103,8 +103,17 @@ class VersionBitsWarningTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
         # is cleared. This will move the versionbit state to ACTIVE.
         self.generatetoaddress(node, VB_PERIOD, node_deterministic_address)
 
+        # The versionbit state is ACTIVE now, so the node has already raised the
+        # unknown rules warning and run -alertnotify.
+        self.wait_until(lambda: self.versionbits_in_alert_file())
+
         # Stop-start the node. This is required because bitcoind will only warn once about unknown versions or unknown rules activating.
-        self.restart_node(0)
+        # Empty the alert file while the node is down, so that the check at the
+        # end of the test can only be satisfied by the alert raised after the restart.
+        self.stop_node(0)
+        with open(self.alert_filename, 'w'):
+            pass
+        self.start_node(0)
 
         # Generating one block guarantees that we'll get out of IBD
         self.generatetoaddress(node, 1, node_deterministic_address)

</patch>
